text:
michael: incident-bot just fired a page to the Ops rotation but I think it targeted the wrong service. PD says PD1234567. 
incident-bot: Page fired -> service: inference-vpc (severity: urgent) | summary: sustained 5xx spike on /v1/generate | link: https://pd.example/PD1234567 :rotating_light:
anya: I’m seeing the same metric alert — but the 5xx is localized to the prod cluster (inference-prod) not inference-vpc. looks like a routing tag mismatch in the PagerDuty rules.
jules: @michael can you confirm who got paged?
michael: Pagerbot trace shows target -> "Ops Night" rotation bound to service inference-vpc. On-call folks who got the page: samir (ack), oncall-manager (CC).
samir: acked this because it came through, but I was confused why PD pointed at vpc. I’m not owning inference-vpc infra atm.
oncall-manager: I did not expect this page either. there's an overlap in the schedule for night contractors that apparently has a shadow binding to inference-vpc.
anya: checking PD routing rules now — looks like a recently-merged rule (PR #4721) added a fallback that maps untagged alerts to inference-vpc. That’s the misconfiguration.
incident-bot: Escalation: 1st -> samir (acked at 1781234620) | 2nd attempt -> oncall-manager (not yet).
michael: customers reporting elevated error rates. I pulled logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T02:10:22Z] svc=inference-prod path=/v1/generate status=502 count=142 window=5m
[2026-03-15T02:11:05Z] svc=inference-prod host=node-23 err=backend-timeout
```
anya: Confirmed — traffic is hitting inference-prod but pager routing sent pages to inference-vpc. So on-call people for inference-prod didn’t get paged.
jules: This explains delayed mitigation. Can we do a temporary manual reroute so inference-prod oncall gets pages for PD1234567?
michael: I’ll open PD reassign to correct service and add a note. Executing now: `pdcli incident assign PD1234567 --service inference-prod --note "manual reroute due to fallback rule"`
incident-bot: Incident PD1234567 reassigned to service inference-prod by michael at 1781234699. Notifications sent.
samir: received new page for inference-prod, acking now.
samir: quick mitigation idea: scale up the inference-prod pool 2x for next 10 minutes to reduce backend timeouts. I can trigger a scale if approved.
oncall-manager: do it. also enable temporary routing to dedicated pool as fallback.
anya: I’m updating the PagerDuty rule to remove the problematic fallback and adding a safety test. Will push PR to revert PR #4721 and add an automated integration test to verify service tags in routing matrix.
michael: mitigation steps executed: 
1) scaled inference-prod by +2 nodes (k8s autoscaler override)
2) enabled dedicated-pool fallback for degraded nodes
3) reassigned PD incident to inference-prod
Status: 5xx rate dropping, customers still affected but improving.
incident-bot: PD1234567 status -> acknowledged (samir) | current severity: urgent | linked alerts: prometheus:inference-5xx-spike (firing)
jules: customer impact summary for support: approx 18% of Gen-API traffic saw 502 between 02:08-02:18 UTC, impacted customers include cid: 9876 (partial), cid: 1123 (timeouts). Support, prepare messaging that we are investigating root cause, mitigation in progress.
oncall-manager: note for postmortem: immediate causes = fallback routing rule + missing tag on alert source; contributing = no automation to verify routing mapping after rule changes.
samir: any ETA on full recovery?
anya: monitoring shows error rate returning to baseline over next 7 minutes; I’ll keep watch. We should keep PD open until 02:40 UTC to ensure stability.
michael: agreed. Action items: 
- anya: revert fallback rule, add test (PR queued)
- samir: run canary for traffic for 15m, confirm tail latencies
- jules: prepare customer comms draft and notify account teams for cids listed
- oncall-manager: runpostmortem owner and timeline after incident closes

jules: draft for support (snippet): "We observed increased 502 responses for inference endpoints between 02:08-02:18 UTC due to an alert-routing misconfiguration. Mitigation applied; cases may have experienced partial failures. We're continuing root cause analysis and will follow up with a postmortem."

michael: thanks all. we should schedule a short blameless postmortem and add a PD routing test to CI. Marking thread for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
